correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 and 1<=i<j<=n, marking independent part sizes in the Euler generating function gives exact p(n) EC_i and p(n) E(C_i C_j) sums, yielding a covariance numerator of differences p(n)p(n-u-v)-p(n-u)p(n-v). For u,v>=2 and positive remainder, the rectangle inequality follows by finite exact 2/3-step bases for t<=25 and strict eventual log concavity from DeSalvo–Pak for larger indices; all lengths >=2 decompose into 2s and 3s. At zero remainder n>=10, Bessenrodt–Ono p(u)p(v)>p(n); n<=9 checked exactly. For i=1, the quotient F(m)=sum_{k<m}p(k)/p(m) is strictly increasing for steps >=2, using ratio comparisons and a finite starting check, forcing each marked covariance summand negative. Summation gives the disjoint part-class claim, not negative association of arbitrary events. Independent exact DP checked 57,155 distinct pair covariances for 2<=n<=70 and 75 base rectangles; universal proof relies on cited infinite partition inequalities.
